texts.preamble: Smt Meenakshi Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 September, 2025 Author: Hirdesh Bench: Hirdesh Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:22492 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Hirdesh On The 16th Of September, 2025 Misc. Petition No. 5090 of 2025 Smt Meenakshi Jain Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh
texts.facts: Brief facts of the case are that Food Safety Officer has inspected the petitioner's firm where the petitioner found present and operating the business of firm. During inspection, the Food Safety Officer found various food articles stored in the shop like Vadapay, Burger, Dabeli which were used for preparing and selling for consumption in the premises. Those articles are found being sub-standard and misbranded, therefore, the Food Safety Officer took the sample of those articles for its analysis to the Public NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:22492 2 MP-5090-2025 Analyst Bhopal from where the same report was prepared wherein the samples of some articles were found misbranded. Thereafter, Foot Safety Officer filed one private complaint before the Adjudicating Officer wherein the show cause notice was issued to the petitioner. Petitioner filed his reply and denied all the allegations. After taking evidence, cost of Rs.50,000/- was imposed upon the petitioner under Section 52 of the Food Safety and Standards Act vide order dated 25.10.2024. Smt Meenakshi Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120271224/ 1 Thereafter, being aggrieved by the order dated 25.10.2024, petitioner filed an appeal before Food Safety Appellate Tribunal along with an application of condonation of delay. Hence, prayed for setting aside the impugned order passed by Appellate Tribunal.
texts.arguments: Being aggrieved by the impugned order of Appellate Tribunal, petitioner filed this petition with submission that impugned order is not in consonance with the spirit of law and only on the ground of limitation the whole appeal ought not to have been dismissed. Petitioner has shown sufficient reasons in the application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of the delay by stating that the copy of the impugned order dated 25.10.2024 has been received by the petitioner on 08.11.2024 and thereafter, petitioner contacted his counsel to prepare the appeal and the same was filed before the Tribunal on 20.01.2025. Thus, the delay of 13 days is bona fide and inadvertent. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State supported the impugned order and prayed for rejection of petition. According to Rule 3.3.1 Food Safety and Standards Act:- Every appeal under Section 70 of the Act arising out of a decision of the Adjudicating Officer appointed under Section 68 of the Act, shall be filed within a period of 30 days from the date on which the copy of the order against which the appeal is filed, is received by the appellant. The Apex Court in the case of N.Balakrishnan Vs. M. Krishnamurthy (1998) 7 SCC 123 in Para 10 and 11 has held as under:- 10. The reason for such a different stance is thus: Smt Meenakshi Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120271224/ 2 The primary function of a court is to adjudicate the dispute between the parties and to advance substantial justice. 11. Rules of limitation are not meant to destroy the rights of parties.
